summary: Policy rollback attestation id is a pure function of (component, target, baseline, policy), and promote()/_apply_policy_promotion treat any existing receipt for that id as the new command's effect, so a recurrent edge replays the old receipt and reports success without moving stable.
failure_scenario: stable v1 -> promote v2 -> registry_rollback(expected_stable=v2, key k1) moves v2->v1 -> promote/rollback back to v2 -> registry_rollback(expected_stable=v2, key k3): plan_rollback_edge yields the same attestation id as k1, promotion_for_attestation finds k1's receipt, validates it (same baseline/target), returns it; command completes 'rolled_back' v2->v1, replayed=False, but stable stays v2 and no promotions row is written.
evidence: Ran a throwaway test through ControlPlane public commands: k1 rolled_back v2->v1 (stable v1); k2 rollback(expected v1) -> reported rolled_back v1->v2 (stable v2); k3 rollback(expected v2) -> reported rolled_back v2->v1, replayed False, stable remained v2; history stayed [(None,v1),(v1,v2),(v2,v1),(v1,v2)] with no 5th edge. Same prior-before-CAS order at runtime/registry.py:734 (library rollback path) and api/_control_commands.py:3195/3213. Existing tests only roll back once per component so never reach the guard. Pre-existing as of this commit.

summary: registry_promote with a previously consumed evaluated attestation, under a new idempotency key, returns the original receipt as a fresh 'promoted' success when stable has since moved back to the attestation's baseline, without moving the pointer.
failure_scenario: attestation A (baseline v1, target v2) promoted v1->v2; rollback to v1; registry_promote(v2, A, key p2): _plan_promotion passes (baseline==current v1), the prior-receipt branch at 1707 validates the old record against the plan and skips the current-stable/CAS check, response is status=promoted v1->v2, replayed=False, while stable is still v1.
evidence: Throwaway test: after rollback v2->v1, registry_promote(AUTHORITY_ACTOR, v2, att, key 'p2') returned PromotionCommandResult promoted v1->v2 replayed False and world._registry.stable_version == v1. No command_id/receipt binding exists, so an exact-command replay is indistinguishable from a new transition. Pre-existing.

summary: registry_promote_initial under a new key accepts a prior bootstrap receipt even when stable has since moved on, and reports 'promoted' with from=None/to=v1 while the pointer is elsewhere.
failure_scenario: v1 initially promoted, v2 promoted; admin calls registry_promote_initial(component, v1, new key): the gate `prior is None and stable is not None` is skipped because the bootstrap receipt exists, _apply_policy_promotion returns it, command completes promoted None->v1 though stable is v2.
evidence: Throwaway test with LOCAL_ADMIN: result status=promoted, from_version None, to_version v1, replayed False, stable_version == v2 (unchanged). Same prior-before-state root cause. Pre-existing.

summary: Rollback target is 'the version before the most recent arrival at current', so rollback of a rollback is a roll-forward onto a version that was just demoted, authorized only by a zero-check policy attestation and labelled rolled_back.
failure_scenario: history (None,v1),(v1,v2),(v2,v1); registry_rollback(expected_stable=v1) selects edge (v2,v1) and moves stable back to v2 with a policy 'rollback' attestation (single synthetic passed check), re-installing a rolled-back candidate without any evaluation, by any PROMOTE_SCOPE actor.
evidence: Throwaway test step k2: rollback(expected v1) returned status rolled_back v1->v2 and stable became v2; history gained (v1,v2). Conflicts with I12/I2 (promotion needs deterministic evaluated proof); the doc only claims 'retained prior version'. Pre-existing.

summary: A planned-but-uncompleted rollback/initial command can be satisfied by another actor's earlier or concurrent receipt for the same edge id, so crash recovery of key K reports success for an effect K never caused.
failure_scenario: Key K planned (v2->v1) then crashes after_plan; meanwhile a different command rolls back v2->v1 and stable later returns to v2; recovering K finds the receipt via attestation id, validates only edge identity, and completes K as rolled_back with stable still v2 (or, if stable is v1, claims credit for another command's effect).
evidence: Derived from code reading plus the same mechanism reproduced above; no command_id/actor is compared in _validate_promotion_receipt (only edge, attestation id, source_run). Crash-interleaving itself not executed.

summary: Rollback and promotion response-loss tests exercise a single transition per component, so no test distinguishes retry of one command from a recurrent baseline-to-candidate edge.
failure_scenario: The v2->v1, v1->v2, v2->v1 sequence and promote-with-consumed-attestation after rollback pass undetected; the only replay assertions use the same key and a stable that has not moved.
evidence: Read test_rollback_recovers_each_response_loss_seam and test_promotion_recovers_each_response_loss_seam; neither re-enters the edge after another transition; confirmed absent by reproduction above. Pre-existing.

summary: Same-key retry of a rollback (plan stored, crash at each seam) recovers with a single mutation and replays the stored response; sqlite store_promotion CAS rejects a stale from_version for fresh attestations.
